questions.prompt: A reads 0; B reads 0; A writes 1; B writes 1 for two increments. What follows?

options.label: The trace can finish at 1; protect the whole read-modify-write transition.
The final value must be 2 because every individual read/write is visible.
Marking the counter volatile makes the increment atomic.

questions.explanation: Visibility of individual reads/writes does not protect their compound transition.

questions.prompt: A is notified about an item, but B consumes it before A reacquires the condition lock. What should A do?

options.label: Recheck the predicate under the reacquired condition lock; notification is not a reserved item.
Consume without checking because notification reserves the item for A.
Assume notify released the lock and gave A exclusive ownership.

questions.explanation: The predicate can cease to hold before the awakened waiter regains the lock.

questions.prompt: Two permits are held. A third worker times out while acquiring. What should its permit cleanup do?

options.label: Do not release: no permit was acquired, and unconditional release corrupts capacity accounting.
Release unconditionally because cleanup must always increase available capacity.
Treat the timeout as success and start work without a permit.

questions.explanation: Cleanup must track successful acquisition; no permit was obtained by the timed-out worker.

questions.prompt: Java SE 17 reports RUNNABLE. What is established?

options.label: RUNNABLE is a JVM state; it does not prove the thread currently owns a CPU.
The thread is necessarily executing on a CPU at this instant.
The enum has a separate RUNNING state that proves simultaneous execution.

questions.explanation: The JVM state does not map directly to operating-system scheduling.

questions.prompt: An old worker in another process resumes after shared ownership changes. Does a mutex in the new worker suffice?

options.label: Use shared authoritative ownership and stale-worker rejection; a local mutex alone cannot fence another process.
Yes; a process-local mutex automatically locks all other processes.
Yes; application authorization alone deduplicates every external effect.

questions.explanation: Coordination scope, authorization and durable effect receipts are independent obligations.
